targets.authors: Walton H, Jr, Miller CM and McCormick II JP
targets.title: Race and political science: the dual traditions of race relations politics and African-American politics
targets.evidence_quote:
We adopt the authors’ typology for distinguishing RRP
and AAP papers, and readers should consult the reference
lists in Walton et al. (1995: Appendix 1) for details.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
By building an instrument that gets at
what Walton and his colleagues observe, we re-analyze
their corpus of text in novel ways and apply our instrument
to current articles in top-tier political science journals.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
This
replication-and-extension confirms not only that ours and
Walton’s operationalizations are empirically comparable
but also that the former can serve as a proxy for the
latter when reviewing the race literature.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original 54-publication corpus is re-analyzed using an alternative automated measure of centrality, rather than rerunning the original numerical analysis. The authors explicitly conclude the operationalizations are comparable and the original findings hold up to re-examination. New journal articles in the extension are not treated as robustness tests of original data.
